proposal.reason: Repair: React element/portal visits are now limited to objects with an own data property key whose value is null, string, number, or bigint. This matches the scoped evidence and frontiers cases that would require library-read getters or unsupported key coercion. As in the installed source, top-level nullish children produce no callback, nested undefined/boolean/hole values are visited as null, strings/numbers/bigints are visited directly, symbols/functions are ignored, arrays recurse left-to-right, callback receiver is forEachContext, callback returns are ignored, and the export returns undefined unless traversal or callback throws.

Repair for size: this smaller program models the observed forEach boundary by recursively traversing supported children, calling the supplied callback with receiver forEachContext and arguments [childOrNull,index], incrementing a shared count, ignoring callback returns, propagating throws, returning undefined, skipping top-level null/undefined, converting nested nullish/boolean/hole values to null, recursing arrays left-to-right, ignoring direct symbol/function children, and accepting ordinary React element or portal objects by $$typeof. Iterator, thenable, lazy, getter-dependent, and other unsupported object cases remain explicit frontiers.
